taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, the US Eastern zone is still on daylight time (EDT = UTC−4), and Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST = UTC+2) — DST in Europe doesn't end until October 25, 2026.

So the offset is 6 hours: 5:00 PM EDT = 21:00 UTC = 23:00 in Madrid, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5 year-round (no daylight saving). So 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026 is 12:00 − 5 hours = 07:00 on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2, so 9:00 AM CEST = 07:00 UTC. Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9 year-round, so add 9 hours: 16:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Convert to UTC:** PDT is UTC−7, so Oct 11, 2026 at 23:59 PDT = Oct 12, 2026 at 06:59 UTC. (PDT is valid then; US DST ends Nov 1, 2026.)

**Step 2 — Convert to Madrid time:** Europe's DST ends on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so on Oct 12 Madrid is still on CEST = UTC+2.

06:59 UTC + 2h = 08:59 on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 – Interpret "PST":** On March 3, 2026, the US West Coast is still on standard time (DST begins March 8, 2026), so PST = UTC−8 is literally correct.

**Step 2 – Convert to UTC:** March 3, 2026, 23:59 PST + 8h = **March 4, 2026, 07:59 UTC**.

**Step 3 – Convert to Madrid time:** Spain switches to summer time on March 29, 2026, so on March 4 Madrid is on CET = UTC+1 → 07:59 + 1h = 08:59 on March 4.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET in early February is UTC+1, so 10:00 CET = 09:00 UTC.

Los Angeles on February 2, 2026 is on PST (UTC−8); US daylight saving doesn't begin until March 8, 2026.

09:00 UTC − 8 hours = 01:00 on February 2, 2026 (same day, Monday).

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9, so 8:00 AM on May 5, 2026 JST = 23:00 UTC on May 4, 2026.

Peru Time (PET) is UTC−5 year-round (no daylight saving), so subtract 5 hours: 18:00 on May 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step by step:**

- Oct 28, 2026 is before US DST ends (Nov 1, 2026), so "PT" = PDT = UTC−7.
- 11:59 PM PDT on Oct 28 → 06:59 UTC on Oct 29, 2026.
- Spain's DST ended Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.
- 06:59 UTC + 1 h = 07:59 on Oct 29, 2026.

Note the catch: Europe falls back a week earlier than the US, so the usual 9-hour gap is 8 hours that week.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- **US DST** ends Nov 1, 2026 (first Sunday in November), so on Oct 30 New York is still on **EDT = UTC−4**.
- 9:00 AM EDT → **13:00 UTC**.
- **EU DST** ended Oct 25, 2026 (last Sunday in October), so Madrid is already on **CET = UTC+1**.
- 13:00 UTC → **14:00 Madrid time**.

(Note the unusual week-long gap where the US is still on DST and Europe isn't — the normal 6-hour offset shrinks to 5 hours.)

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Is "CET" literal here?** Europe's summer time ends on the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is **October 25**. So by October 27, Central Europe really is on CET = UTC+1. The label checks out.

**Step 2 — Convert to UTC:** 18:00 − 1 h = **17:00 UTC**.

**Step 3 — Convert to New York:** US daylight time ends the first Sunday of November, i.e. **November 1, 2026**. So October 27 is still EDT = UTC−4.
17:00 UTC − 4 h = **13:00 EDT**.

So you have until 1:00 PM on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 — note the unusual 5-hour (not 6-hour) offset, since Europe has switched off DST but the US hasn't yet.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- US daylight saving time ends Sunday, **Nov 1, 2026**, so on Nov 2 the Pacific zone is **PST = UTC−8**.
- Nov 2, 2026, 23:59 PST → **Nov 3, 2026, 07:59 UTC**.
- EU daylight saving ends Sunday, **Oct 25, 2026**, so Madrid is on **CET = UTC+1**.
- 07:59 UTC + 1 h → **Nov 3, 2026, 08:59** Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — What is "PT" on March 20, 2026?**
US daylight saving time began Sunday, March 8, 2026, so Pacific Time is PDT = UTC−7.
→ March 20, 2026, 23:59 PDT = March 21, 2026, 06:59 UTC.

**Step 2 — Convert to Madrid time.**
EU summer time starts the last Sunday of March (March 29, 2026), so Madrid is still on CET = UTC+1.
→ 06:59 UTC + 1h = 07:59 on March 21, 2026.

So the contest closes Saturday morning, March 21, 2026, at 7:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Interpret "CET":** CET = UTC+1. On March 25, 2026, Europe hasn't switched to summer time yet (that happens March 29, 2026), so UTC+1 is correct as stated.

12:00 CET → **11:00 UTC**

**Step 2 — Convert to Los Angeles:** US daylight saving time began March 8, 2026, so LA is on PDT = UTC−7.

11:00 UTC − 7h = **04:00 on March 25, 2026**

So the webinar starts at 4:00 AM Wednesday morning your time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Interpret "12:00 AM ET":** 12:00 AM means midnight at the *start* of October 12, 2026.

**Step 2 — Which ET offset?** US daylight saving time in 2026 runs March 8 – November 1, so October 12 is EDT = UTC−4.
→ 2026-10-12 00:00 EDT = 2026-10-12 04:00 UTC.

**Step 3 — Convert to Madrid:** EU summer time runs until the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Madrid is on CEST = UTC+2.
→ 04:00 UTC + 2h = 06:00 on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Convert AoE to UTC.** Anywhere on Earth (AoE) is UTC−12. So October 9, 2026, 23:59 AoE = October 10, 2026, 11:59 UTC.

**Step 2 — Convert UTC to Madrid time.** European summer time (CEST, UTC+2) runs until the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 25. October 10 is still CEST, so add 2 hours: 13:59 on October 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- "12:00 PM PT" on August 14, 2026 = noon Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7), since US DST runs March 8 – November 1 in 2026.
- Noon PDT = 19:00 UTC.
- Madrid in mid-August is on CEST (UTC+2), as EU summer time runs until October 25, 2026.
- 19:00 UTC + 2 h = 21:00 on the same day, Friday, August 14, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Interpreting "IST" as India Standard Time (UTC+5:30)** — the most common usage for contest pages.

- Deadline: 2026‑11‑10, 23:59 IST → 18:29 UTC (subtract 5:30).
- Madrid in November is on CET (UTC+1); DST ended Oct 25, 2026.
- 18:29 UTC + 1:00 = 19:29 on Nov 10, 2026.

(Caveat: if "IST" meant Israel Standard Time (UTC+2), it would be 22:59 Madrid time; if Irish time, Ireland is on GMT in November, so 00:59 on Nov 11.)

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Convert Nepal time to UTC.**
Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45 (no daylight saving).
17:00 − 5:45 = **11:15 UTC on April 2, 2026**

**Step 2 — Convert UTC to Lima time.**
Peru Time (PET) is UTC−5 year-round (Peru does not observe DST).
11:15 − 5:00 = **06:15 on April 2, 2026**

So you'd need to submit by 6:15 AM on April 2 — an early morning deadline, since Nepal is 10 hours 45 minutes ahead of Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Adelaide offset on Oct 6, 2026:** Australian daylight saving starts the first Sunday in October = Oct 4, 2026. So Adelaide is on ACDT = UTC+10:30.

**Step 2 — Convert to UTC:** 10:00 on Oct 6 minus 10:30 = 23:30 UTC on Oct 5, 2026.

**Step 3 — Convert to Madrid:** Spain is on CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026). So 23:30 UTC + 2h = 01:30 on Oct 6, 2026.

So you must apply by 1:30 AM on the night of Oct 5–6 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney on Oct 3, 2026 is still on standard time (AEST, UTC+10) — DST begins Sunday, Oct 4, 2026.

- 6:00 PM AEST = 08:00 UTC on Oct 3
- Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) until Oct 25, 2026 → 10:00 local

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
